inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 229.56m ordinary shares outstanding at 2026-10-26 (Q1 FY2027 10-Q cover) plus ~2.5m employee-award dilution, consistent with the 232m diluted weighted count in the Q1 FY2027 EPS note. The 2028 Exchangeable Notes were fully exchanged by 2026-09-08 and their shares are already in the basic count. Held FLAT because SBC (incl. net-settlement taxes) is expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation $213m plus $119m taxes paid on net share settlement of equity awards (financing). Seagate publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. Interest income ($30m) NOT stripped: the company is in net debt.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD-built rate: ~4.3% 10y UST + ~4.5-5% ERP x beta ~1.3 for a cyclical hardware oligopolist gives cost of equity ~10.5%; debt is now under 2% of enterprise value so WACC ~10%. The SAME 10% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, customer concentration and capacity risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not a second time in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases are already expensed inside EBITDA; lease liabilities ($62m, FY2026 10-K) are excluded from net debt. One treatment, no adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the cyclical adaptations (operating company; HDD manufacturer - not a bank/REIT/holdco). First valuation of this ticker. NORMALISATION: FY0 is FY2026 (revenue $12.2bn) but the business is at a cyclical peak - September-2026 quarter revenue $4.23bn at 57.3% gross margin and ~52% pre-SBC EBITDA margin versus a FY2010-FY2022 range of ~15-26% EBITDA margin on $10-15bn revenue. Year 1 (FY2027) is anchored to the Q1 actual and the Q2 guide ($4.8bn, non-GAAP EPS $9.20); thereafter every scenario runs a digestion phase and settles at a stated mid-cycle margin rather than capitalising the run-rate. The terminal value is capitalised on year-10 mid-cycle FCF, never on peak FCF. NET DEBT is PRO FORMA: $2,372m principal and $1,258m cash at 2026-10-02, adjusted for the 2026-10-15 redemption of $750m of 2032 Notes (cash out ~$831m including the ~$81m loss management flagged). BUYBACKS: $176m in FY2026 and $400m in Q1 FY2027, with a step-up signalled for calendar 2027 under a $4.4bn remaining authorisation - the flat share count is being funded. CASH TAX: FY2026 cash taxes paid were only $40m against a $506m provision; the gap sits in a $706m long-term Pillar Two tax payable, which is deducted in the equity bridge while forward flows carry a full 15-16% cash tax, so historical reported FCF (and last_fcf) overstates sustainable cash generation by roughly the unpaid tax. DATA NOTE: the Metrics row labelled 'Q2 2027' is a mislabelled Q2 FY2026 balance sheet (equity 459, debt 4,499) and was ignored.

equity_bridge.note: Q1 FY2027 10-Q liquidity section: ~$706m long-term tax payable for Pillar Two global minimum tax; accrued, not yet paid, and not in the forward cash-tax path

equity_bridge.note: Q1 FY2027 10-Q: $210m accrued (securities class action $175m and remaining BIS instalments), less ~$70m of the class action covered by insurers

$1.5bn notional capped calls remain outstanding after the notes were exchanged (10-Q note 3); cap price $107.74 vs an exchange price near $82.5 on ~18.2m shares gives ~$460m at the cap, taken at ~$400m for time value and counterparty risk. Estimate: the exchange price is from the 2023 offering terms, not restated in the latest filing

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: through-cycle revenue growth (10-year revenue CAGR FY2016-FY2026 is 0.9%, 5-year 2.7%) plus mid-single-digit exabyte-led growth after the cycle normalises
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is not usable as the growth anchor: shareholders' equity was negative FY2023-FY2025 (buyback-driven deficit) and the FY2021-FY2026 figure of 28% is a rebound through zero. 3-year EPS and equity CAGRs are undefined (negative FY2023 base). All trailing CAGRs are trough-to-peak (FY2023 revenue $7.4bn, FY2026 $12.2bn) and overstate sustainable growth.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less equity-award taxes; interest income not stripped, net debt throughout), $m: FY2020 980, FY2021 983, FY2022 1,080, FY2023 467, FY2024 499, FY2025 564, FY2026 2,773. Owner-FCF CAGRs (3yr 81%, 5yr 23%) track reported FCF (3yr 71%, 5yr 22%) - SBC is ~2-3% of revenue and is not growing faster than cash flow. FY2026 FCF is flattered by ~$465m of Pillar Two tax accrued but not paid.

base.rationale: FY2027 revenue ~$18.9bn = Q1 actual $4.23bn + Q2 guide $4.8bn + ~$4.9-5.0bn per quarter in H2 on sold-out nearline capacity. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin 54.5% from Q1 actual ~52% and the ~54-55% implied by the Q2 EPS guide. Mid-cycle margin 40% (gross margin ~45%, opex ~9%) is roughly double the pre-2023 norm - it credits the oligopoly, build-to-order pricing and HAMR cost-down, but not shortage pricing (~$19/TB now vs $14-15 in FY2024-25). Capex at the stated 4-6% of revenue; D&A converges up toward capex. Cash tax at the 15% Pillar Two floor. Working capital consumes ~10% of revenue growth (receivables + inventory less payables is ~10% of annualised revenue) and releases in the down years.

scenario_narratives.base: The AI nearline shortage runs through FY2028 - revenue peaks near $21bn at ~55% EBITDA margin - and then the industry does what it has done after every prior tightness: hyperscalers digest inventory, Toshiba and Western Digital capacity arrives, and price per terabyte resumes its decline. Revenue falls ~15% over FY2029-30 and then grows 3-5% on ~20% exabyte growth net of price erosion. The structural change is kept, not the shortage: three suppliers, build-to-order contracts and HAMR cost-down hold mid-cycle EBITDA margin at 40%, about twice the pre-2023 level, with capex inside the 4-6% target.
scenario_narratives.bull: Supply discipline holds across all three HDD makers and AI data retention keeps nearline exabyte demand growing 25%+ with no digestion year: revenue reaches ~$23bn in FY2028 and compounds to ~$36bn by FY2036. Mozaic/HAMR areal-density gains let cost per terabyte fall faster than price, so today's margin is largely structural - EBITDA margin settles at 50%, with SSDs failing to reach cost parity in mass-capacity tiers. This needs both sustained hyperscaler capex and continued capacity restraint by competitors.
scenario_narratives.bear: A classic HDD cycle. Hyperscaler AI capex slows or customers find they double-ordered into the shortage; Toshiba's expansion and WD's HAMR ramp break pricing; the one ~14% customer uses its leverage. Revenue falls from ~$18bn to ~$12bn by FY2030 (the FY2023 correction was -37% in one year) and under-absorption drags EBITDA margin back to 26-27% - still above the 15-21% of FY2016-FY2022 because the mix is now 80% data center. Enterprise SSDs take share at the low end of nearline and Edge IoT keeps shrinking, leaving 2-3% growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25%: margins are at an all-time peak in a business with a long record of sharp reversals, one customer is ~14% of revenue, and Toshiba has announced capacity expansion - though there is no solvency risk after $2.6bn+ of debt reduction. Base 50%: a normal cycle around a structurally better oligopoly margin. Bull cut to 25%: it needs two independent things to hold for a decade - hyperscaler AI capex and capacity restraint by both competitors.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Seagate is valued on mid-cycle owner FCF, not on the September-2026 run-rate. The two peak years (FY2027-28) are counted in full as cash, but the terminal value capitalises a normalised year-10 flow at a cyclical multiple (12-16x). SBC and net-settlement taxes are expensed, the share count is flat, the accrued-but-unpaid Pillar Two tax is deducted as a liability, and one discount rate is used across scenarios so cyclicality is charged once, in the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin is the dominant unknown: each 5pp of terminal EBITDA margin moves the base value by roughly 10%, and there is no completed cycle under the new industry structure to calibrate against
Timing and depth of the nearline digestion phase - the base case assumes it starts in FY2029; a longer shortage adds peak-year cash, an earlier one removes it
Competitor capacity additions (Toshiba expansion, WD HAMR ramp) ending supply discipline
Customer concentration: one customer ~14% of revenue, three customers 44% of receivables
SSD cost-per-TB convergence in mass-capacity tiers over the 10-year horizon
Cash tax: FY2026 paid $40m against a $506m provision; the model assumes the Pillar Two 15% rate is paid in cash going forward and the $706m payable is settled
